title: HIV Diagnostic Algorithms: Window Period and Testing
subject: Microbiology
preview: Modern HIV testing commonly uses antigen-antibody assays followed by a defined supplemental testing algorithm.
quickRevision: Modern HIV testing commonly uses antigen-antibody assays followed by a defined supplemental testing algorithm.
A single rapid test result must be interpreted under the approved national diagnostic strategy.
Counseling, linkage to care and repeat testing when indicated are part of safe practice.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Modern HIV testing commonly uses antigen-antibody assays followed by a defined supplemental testing algorithm.
Very early infection may have a diagnostic window period; nucleic acid testing may be appropriate in selected cases.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: A single rapid test result must be interpreted under the approved national diagnostic strategy.
Counseling, linkage to care and repeat testing when indicated are part of safe practice.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not exclude very recent HIV acquisition solely from one early negative antibody-only result.

quiz.question: What explains an early negative HIV antibody test after recent exposure?
quiz.explanation: Window period before detectable antibodies. Very early infection may have a diagnostic window period; nucleic acid testing may be appropriate in selected cases.
